semester: 3rd Semester (Winter Semester start); 2nd Semester (Summer Semester start)
prerequisites: Language skills at B1/B2 level according to CEF recommended; voluntary self-assessment test

learning_outcomes.text: To use vocabulary from the fields of Business English, technology, technologies, physics, mechanical engineering, materials, engineering, renewable energies.
To apply linguistic means of the business world as well as for describing, discussing, arguing, narrating, logical linking, moderating.
To acquire knowledge, vocabulary, and structures through English texts/articles and subsequently comment on, pass on, reproduce, and evaluate them.
To use the English language grammatically correctly.

syllabus_topics: Vocabulary in the aforementioned economic and technical areas - through specialist articles and original English sources.
Confident written and oral expression through workshops: business writing, presenting, conversation, business situations, academic writing.
Idiomatic expression, linguistic correctness, communication training – language is a tool
teaching_methods: Seminar-style language training with lecture phases

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam part: case study presentation

assessment_rules: The overall examination consists of a written exam (90 min) and an oral examination part (case study presentation, 20%). The module is graded based on the passed examination performance. The weighting for the final grade is determined by ECTS credits.
bibliography: Current textbooks Business English, Technical English, current specialist articles, press sources (e.g. The Guardian, The Independent, The New York Times, Scientific American, Mechanical Engineering Magazine, The Economist), BBC documentaries, Google Tech Talks
Strutt, Peter: Market Leader: Essential Business Grammar and Usage, Longman, 2010.
